prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (within 500 words)

Core aims
- Freeze most immigration; end illegal Channel crossings through detention, deportation, and potential returns to France; create a new immigration department; leave the European Convention on Human Rights.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use; expand use of independent capacity; offer tax incentives and staffing reforms.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; cut energy taxes and scrap green levies; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Large savings from cutting government waste, halving foreign aid, and stopping interest on QE reserves.

Tax and economy
- Personal: Lift income tax start point to £20,000; higher-rate threshold to £70,000; cut fuel duty by 20p; remove VAT and levies on energy; cut stamp duty (0% to £750k); restore VAT-free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax (0% below £2m, 20% above with charity option).
- Business: Exempt profits up to £100k from corporation tax; reduce main rate to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT registration threshold to £150k; abolish high-street business rates, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; deregulation and planning reform; simplify tax code.

Immigration and borders
- Freeze non-essential routes (healthcare as key exception); bar student dependents; five-year residency and employment for benefits; employer National Insurance surcharge of 20% for foreign workers (with exemptions); immediate deportation of foreign offenders after sentences.

NHS and social care
- Zero basic-rate income tax for frontline NHS and care staff for three years; remove training caps; partial student fee write-off tied to service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare and insurance; patient vouchers if access targets missed; efficiency measures; inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
  
Energy and environment
- Scrap Net Zero obligations and renewable subsidies (replace with taxes on subsidies); fast-track North Sea oil and gas and shale pilots; pursue small modular nuclear reactors and other technologies.

Law and order, justice
- Recruit 40,000 police over five years; “zero tolerance” approach; higher use of stop and search; tougher sentences for violent and drug crimes; streamline leadership; reduce non-operational roles.
- Justice: mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; raise budget to reduce backlogs; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 detention places; reforms on child maintenance, grooming gangs, and youth offender training.

Education and benefits
- Curriculum changes; restrictions on gender-related policies in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; tighter university entry and shorter degree options; expand Pupil Referral Units.
- Benefits: stricter work requirements (two-offer rule), face-to-face assessments, training and apprenticeships.

Other policy areas
- Brexit/regulation: rescind retained EU laws; revise NI arrangements; prepare for trade renegotiations.
- Defence: spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay review; new veterans department; procurement reform; recruit 30,000 army personnel.
- Housing: faster brownfield planning; social housing priority for locals; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; leasehold protections.
- Families: transferable marriage allowance when affordable; front-load child benefit for ages 1–4; single-sex facilities; smartphone harms inquiry.
- Transport/utilities: cancel remaining HS2; remove ULEZ/LTNs; no bans on petrol/diesel cars; mixed public–pension fund ownership model for utilities; cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/fisheries: increase farm budget to £3bn; shift subsidies to production; tackle supermarket power; “buy British” targets; license foreign fishing, expand patrols, ban supertrawlers, rebuild processing.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; address offshore tax practices in care homes; review pension system; change Mineworkers Pension Scheme surplus rules.
- Constitutional/civil sphere: leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; new Bill of Rights; replace equalities framework; free speech bill; BBC licence reform; anti-corruption unit.

Funding (as claimed)
- Annual savings: approx. £150bn, plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn.
- Annual costs: approx. £141bn.
